statement: (i) Prove that $\sin 3\theta = 3\sin\theta-4\sin^{3}\theta$. (ii) Hence solve $8\sin^{3}\theta-6\sin\theta+1=0$ for $0\le\theta\le\pi$. (iii) Show that among the solutions there is exactly one in $(0,\frac{\pi}{6})$.
solution: (i) $\sin 3\theta=\sin(2\theta+\theta)=\sin2\theta\cos\theta+\cos2\theta\sin\theta=2\sin\theta\cos^{2}\theta+(1-2\sin^{2}\theta)\sin\theta=2\sin\theta(1-\sin^{2}\theta)+\sin\theta-2\sin^{3}\theta=3\sin\theta-4\sin^{3}\theta$. (ii) Using the identity, $8\sin^{3}\theta-6\sin\theta=-2\sin 3\theta$, so the equation becomes $-2\sin 3\theta+1=0\Rightarrow \sin 3\theta=\frac12$. For $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, $3\theta\in[0,3\pi]$: $3\theta=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6},\frac{13\pi}{6},\frac{17\pi}{6}$, giving $\theta=\frac{\pi}{18},\frac{5\pi}{18},\frac{13\pi}{18},\frac{17\pi}{18}$. (iii) $\frac{\pi}{18}<\frac{\pi}{6}$ and each of the others exceeds $\frac{\pi}{6}$, so exactly one lies in $(0,\frac{\pi}{6})$.
hints: Rewrite the cubic using the triple-angle identity.
